findings.message:
[P1] Preserve the Edit button when rebuilding key actions

`editBtn` is appended to `actionRow`, then `renderKeyActions` immediately clears the row with `textContent = ""` and only adds revoke/restore/delete controls. Every API-key row therefore loses its Edit button, preventing expiry and other key edits.

static/admin.js:6833-6833

[P1] Make the API-key test match and exercise behavior

This assertion requires `if (statusKind !== "revoked")`, but the implementation uses `if (nextStatusKind !== "revoked")`, so the new test fails every run. Even after correcting that name, the surrounding checks only match source text rather than rendering a row or exercising delayed saves, confirmation cancellation, or the unrevoke warning.

tests/static-assets.test.ts:811-811

[P2] Cover revoke and unrevoke in the cache matrix

The route matrix jumps from `/admin/api-keys/changes` to kernel routes and omits the defined `POST /admin/api-keys/revoke` and `POST /admin/api-keys/unrevoke` endpoints, so a cache-header regression on either mutation route would pass the purported route-wide test.

tests/static-assets.test.ts:768-773

summary: The patch introduces an API-key editing regression and a failing, incomplete test suite.

evidence: `renderKeyActions` clears the action row after the Edit button is appended, so API-key rows cannot be edited and the expiry-edit requirement is not fulfilled.
The new API-key test expects `statusKind` while the implementation uses `nextStatusKind`, making the test fail; its source-text assertions also do not implement the requested behavioral tests.
The route-wide cache test omits the revoke and unrevoke admin endpoints.
